2 هجّر , (Lth, A, K, &c.,) inf. n. تَهْجِيرٌ, (S, Msb, K,) He journeyed in the time called the هَاجِرَة; (Lth, S, A, Mgh, K;) as also ↓ تهجّر ; (IAar, S, A, K;) and ↓ اهجر : (K:) or he went forth in that time: (Az, TA:) or he was (صَارَ) in that time: (Msb: [but in my copy of that work, صار is perhaps a mistake for سَارَ:]) or ↓ اهجر has this last signification; (Lth, TA;) or signifies he entered upon that time; like اظهر (A.) ―
-b2- It (the day) attained to the time called he هَاجِرَة. (S, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
